mcqs.q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
options: Mass is the amount of matter (kg); weight is the gravitational force on that mass (N) and depends on g.
Mass and weight are the same thing, just expressed in different units.
The lighter ball falls faster because it has less inertia.
Mass changes with location but weight does not.

mcqs.q: If air resistance is ignored, which falls faster: a heavy ball or a light ball dropped from the same height?
options: The water turns into wave material and changes state.
Both fall at the same rate because gravitational acceleration is independent of mass.
The lighter ball falls faster because it has less inertia.
Heavier objects fall faster than lighter objects because gravity pulls more on them.

mcqs.q: When a wave travels through water, what happens to the water itself?
options: The water oscillates about a fixed point; the wave transfers energy, not matter.
The water moves along with the wave from one place to another.
The water turns into wave material and changes state.
The lighter ball falls faster because it has less inertia.
